notes: clear() on an undivided tree (line 244 branch false) only runs points.length=0 and is hit incidentally by afterEach release; the inert reset cannot regress observably.

KillHandler.test and AssignBodiesBatch tests never set an owner with assignment.assignedIds, so the 'owner does not reference bodyId, leave untouched' path (line 19) is genuinely unpinned and a regression could wipe unrelated owners' assignments.
The no-draft return (line 16) is exercised incidentally by the restore tests' draftless sys_world, and a regression would at worst add an inert active:false draft object with no behavioral effect.
Tests use count 2,4,7,40 and never count==6, so the count<=SMALL_SWARM_LIMIT ring-vs-spiral flip is untested, but the boundary only selects one cosmetic layout for one crowd size.
GlyphRegistry.advanced.test never drives nextOrdinal to MAX_GLYPH_CAPACITY, so the capacity-exhaustion throw at the ==MAX boundary (line 102) is untested.
Module tests use pointer distances of 400 (null) and 100/160 (visible) but never distance==200, yet at the boundary alpha computes to 0 so returning null vs a zero-alpha light is visually identical.
The 'returns null for degenerate paths' test already covers pathLengthPx=0 (< ZERO_LENGTH_PX); the 0.001 epsilon is a degeneracy guard where no meaningful path length lands exactly on the boundary.
ParticlesConfigRegistry.test only calls heat mapIntensity(0.5) and asserts property presence, so the intensity<HEAT_THRESHOLD enabled/disabled flip at ==0.1 is untested.
ParticlesConfigRegistry.test only calls xp mapIntensity(0) and asserts property presence, so the intensity<XP_THRESHOLD enabled/disabled flip at ==0.05 is untested.
No test imports computeSeek/applySeek from Steering.ts (only ImpulseSteeringForces, a different module, is tested), so the len<=MIN_DISTANCE zero-vector boundary and the whole function are untested.

The stack-overflow regression test drives subdivision toward the guard but no test pins width==MIN_EXTENT, and this is a genuine recursion-termination boundary where <= vs < changes how deep subdivision goes.
total is a sum of clamped non-negative amounts and line 44 already returns when total<=0, so total<MIN_TRANSFER_THRESHOLD (0) at line 51 is unreachable dead code with no boundary risk.

The only reference to MAX_RUNTIME_SUBSTEPS in tests is a comment that deliberately avoids the cap by ticking individually, so no test asserts the steps==MAX_RUNTIME_SUBSTEPS substep-cap behavior (loop exit and return 0).
